Trans rights groups raised concerns, while sex-based rights groups welcomed the change.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: NHS England published updated guidance requiring hospital wards, toilets and changing rooms to be used based on biological sex rather than gender identity. Where single-sex accommodation is not clinically appropriate, alternative arrangements must ensure patient dignity and safety. Clinical needs remain the overriding priority in emergency and urgent care settings.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The update follows a Supreme Court judgment ruling that sex and woman under equality law refer to biological sex. Sex-based rights charity Sex Matters welcomed the shift, while trans rights organisations warned the rules will create unworkable operational challenges in resource-strapped hospitals. Recent employment tribunals also highlighted legal disputes over single-sex changing facilities for hospital staff.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: NHS trusts are encouraged to audit staff facilities to ensure accessible alternatives like gender-neutral or single-occupancy spaces are provided, while an appeal regarding NHS Fife changing room rules is expected in court next year.

gist: Major carmakers' electric battery supplies were linked to rainforest deforestation in Indonesia.
Nickel mined in Sulawesi is processed in China before reaching automotive battery factories.
Indigenous Tolaki lands face environmental harm while carmakers pledge audits and supply chain reviews.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An investigation revealed that nickel from the Cahaya and Hengjaya mines in Sulawesi, Indonesia, enters supply chains for carmakers including Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla. The ore is processed locally and in China by Huayou before reaching battery manufacturers such as CATL. Satellite data shows mining has caused extensive deforestation on indigenous Tolaki lands.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Carmakers use nickel in cathodes to boost battery range, but increased mining threatens primary rainforests and biodiversity. Forest loss from mining operations may multiply nickel's carbon footprint up to 500 times compared with earlier estimates, while also harming local indigenous livelihoods.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Global nickel demand is projected to double by 2040. Carmakers including Ford stated they are reviewing the findings, while Volvo Cars plans further supplier audits in 2026 and beyond.
